sections.kicker: Prepared for Hairbrella by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Hairbrella is named for the idea of an umbrella for hair. The hero sells a scarf.
sections.keep: Two women with different hair textures, each framed by the product. They show who this is for.

pins.area: The hero headline reads Superior Warmth Ultimate Protection above the new infinity rain scarf
pins.what: The hero sells warmth and a new scarf. The name promises protection for hair.
pins.why: Hairbrella is a strong idea in the name. The headline drops it for a product feature.
pins.how: Lead with the idea in the name and let the scarf prove it.
pins.label: Your hero
pins.cost: A visitor sees a scarf. They do not see the idea that makes you Hairbrella.

pins.area: Both models wear black hoods and black tops against a pale grey backdrop
pins.what: Both models wear black hoods and black tops against a pale grey backdrop.
pins.why: The product disappears into the wardrobe, and the brand pink of the button is nowhere in the photo.
pins.how: Put the brand colour into the photograph and let the product stand out.
pins.label: Your photos
pins.cost: The product is hard to see in the picture that sells it.

pins.area: The soft lowercase hairbrella wordmark sits above a headline in heavy black capitals
pins.what: The wordmark is a soft lowercase. The headline under it is heavy black capitals.
pins.why: The logo and the headline sound like two different brands.
pins.how: Choose the voice that sounds like you and carry it through.
pins.label: Your type
pins.cost: The brand has no single voice for people to remember.
